High-level ask from your side was: additional reserved GPUs to handle concurrent bursts and an explicit throughput SLA for peak 2-hour windows.

- Warm pool: 2 warm replicas kept idle for < 30s cold-starts
- Autoscale: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=12, scale_up_target=60s median to provision new replica under normal load
- Throughput guarantee: 40k tokens/min sustained for the reserved pool during 2-hour peak windows

I've attached an initial_capacity_summary.pdf with the expected cost delta and a simple throughput model. If this looks close to what you had in mind, I can loop in Rishi and Marissa to firm up the policy language and update the SOW.

Neha / Rishi / Anna —

Thanks for the context. Below is the autoscale policy language I propose for the SOW; I've also attached a short matrix (autoscale_policy_matrix.xlsx) with billing implications and example traffic curves.

Proposed autoscale policy (SOW language):
- Reserved pool: +4 A100-equivalent GPUs dedicated to FastRetail, billed to the committed line item for the renewal term. Warm pool is considered capacity within the reserved commitment and is not a separate billable standby line item.
- Warm pool semantics: maintain 2 warm replicas (vm pre-warmed, container & model initialized). Warm replicas can be used to absorb sudden bursts without triggering cold-starts; warm pool counts toward reserved capacity minimum.
- Min/Max replicas: min_replicas = 2 (always), max_replicas = 12 for the dedicated tenant cluster. Autoscaling respects both request concurrency and token-rate; scale decisions use rolling 60s windows.
- Scale-up latency target: goal = 60s median for adding a new replica under sustained load; max allowed lag (for SLA measurement) = 90s. If scale-up exceeds 90s for >30 minutes during a declared peak window, customer is eligible for the throughput SLA credit.
- Scale-down behavior: cooldown = 300s after last scale activity; warm replicas may be retained between peaks per mutually agreed schedule.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to a lower-capacity but compatible model variant if cluster is saturated; routing used only if customer enables fallback in Console.

Notes:
- For the holiday peak we recommend increasing reserved pool to +6 temporarily (burstable addendum) if FastRetail expects >2x baseline concurrency. We can include a temporary uplift clause in the SOW (30-day notice) to avoid late procurement delays.
- Billing: warm pool included in reserved commit; credits for SLA outages are calculated as a percentage of the monthly reserved fee (standard: 10% credit for qualifying 30-minute outage, capped at 100% of monthly fee).

Attachments: autoscale_policy_matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)

Happy to iterate; if this looks good I'll update the SOW and send for signature.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
